description: Crafted text in an application note or retrieved document steers the model's proposal (prompt injection).
A retrieved document carries an instruction the agent follows.
A persisted memory entry poisons a later run.
A tool result or preview exposes more customer data than the task needed.
Malformed, oversized or duplicate-key requests reach the HTTP boundary.
Third-party tool metadata or a dependency carries a hostile instruction or code.
The Ollama image is pulled by a floating tag, so a re-pushed image changes the model runtime silently.
Anything that reaches the container network can call AcmeBank and the Attack Service, which authenticate no callers themselves.
A fail-open ALLOW raises no alert, so silence is read as safety.
Telemetry is a second copy of runtime events; anything placed in an event is readable by whoever can search the index.
Forged or altered telemetry makes an investigation reach the wrong conclusion.
Changing the coded policy, or forging an allow ticket, changes every authorization decision. (Custom: the article's Layer 6 threats concern AI security agents, and AcmeBank has none.)
An agent requests a tool, scope or resource it was not granted.
A claimed identity or delegation is treated as if it were authority.
An instruction changes what an authorized tool is used for.
A tool result or catalog description becomes authority for the next call.
